data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Sorting networks operate in parallel/comparator-based, unlike typical DP which is sequential.","Optimal substructure is not guaranteed for minimal sorting networks, as minimal networks for larger n might not contain minimal networks for smaller n as prefixes."],"overturn_conditions":["Exhaustive or SAT-based search proves no 45-comparator network contains an S(10) prefix.","A 45-comparator network is found that demonstrably does not contain any S(10) prefix within its first 29 comparators."],"shared_structure":["Both involve fixing a substructure of known optimal size and recursively/iteratively solving the remainder.","Both rely on the optimal substructure property being present in the final optimal solution."],"source_memory_refs":["algorithmic_optimal_substructure_dp","sorting_network_n_prefix_extension"],"transfer_claims":["If the minimal S(13) network contains an optimal S(10) prefix, the decomposition search will find it exponentially faster than exhaustive search."]},"claim":"A search strategy decomposing the 13-input problem into an optimal S(10)=29 comparator prefix followed by a 16-comparator integration phase will discover a 45-comparator network if one exists with this structural decomposition, and will outperform undirected random search in finding sub-48 comparator networks.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the minimal S(13) network does not contain an optimal S(10) prefix (i.e., the first 29 comparators do not sort channels 0-9 completely), this strategy will miss the optimal 44 or 45 comparator network.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the integration of the 3 extra channels inherently requires more than 16 comparators when constrained by a 10-channel prefix, this method yields a lower bound > 45.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The search space of 13-input networks is vast. By mandating that the first 29 comparators form the known optimal S(10) network on channels 0-9, we structurally constrain the search to the remaining 16 comparators. These remaining comparators must sort the 3 new channels and integrate them with the sorted prefix, which reduces the branching factor. The 0-1 principle (8192 vectors) evaluates candidate completions in milliseconds.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
